h: Mummies, River Walks and Bouncing Know-How
p: Got a first-timer in the group? Trampoline parks can feel a bit overwhelming when you walk in, with music thumping and kids flying in every direction. Give newcomers a few minutes to find their feet on a quieter bed before diving into the busiest areas. Confidence builds fast, and before long they'll be the ones dragging you back for one more go.

Practical bits: fill in the waiver online before you set off, keep grip socks for next time, and pack a drink and a light snack for afterwards. Leave jewellery at home and lock phones away, as they have a habit of flying out of pockets mid-bounce.

Maidstone has a good mix of things to do once you're done. Maidstone Museum, right in the town centre, has a surprising collection that includes an Egyptian mummy, natural history displays and local history, and it's a great follow-up for curious kids. The River Medway runs through the heart of town, and the riverside path is a pleasant place to stroll, with boats moored along the bank.

Follow the river north and you'll reach Aylesford, a pretty village with a medieval bridge and The Friars, a peaceful Carmelite priory with gardens open to visitors. To the north of Maidstone, the Kent Downs offer big views and great walking, while the Hazlitt Theatre in town puts on shows throughout the year. Between them, it's easy to turn a trampoline session into a full Kent day out.
